# Emily K. Johnson

[Assistant Professor, [Danish Centre for Health Economics](https://www.sdu.dk/en/dache)<br>Visiting Fellow, [Danish Institute for Advanced Study](https://www.sdu.dk/en/dias)<br>University of Southern Denmark]{.hero-role}

::: {.lead}
I study how we measure population health, and I work to improve what large administrative datasets can tell us about health outcomes and their consequences.
:::

People are living longer but spending more of that time in poor health, societies are ageing while fertility declines, and multimorbidity makes disease burden hard to quantify. Much of my work asks what poor health costs individuals and societies in this setting, both in healthcare spending and in the long-term economic and social consequences of disease.

## Background

::: {.background}

::: {.background-col}

### Positions

::: {.bg-item}
**University of Southern Denmark** [2026 – present]{.bg-date}

Assistant Professor, Danish Centre for Health Economics, and Visiting Fellow, Danish Institute for Advanced Study. Register-based research on the economic and social consequences of disease, and comparisons of health expenditure and resource use across countries.
:::

::: {.bg-item}
**Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation** [2019 – 2023]{.bg-date}

Research Scientist. Clinical informatics for the Global Burden of Disease study and disease expenditure estimation for US counties. Led the integration of Medicare and Medicaid claims data for IHME research.
:::

::: {.bg-item}
**Epic Systems** [2017 – 2019]{.bg-date}

Technical Services. Supported electronic health record implementations of population health management programs for large health systems.
:::
